name: George Knott Reserve
summary: A measured option for inner-north intervals. Yarra allows community use outside club activities and events; Collingwood Harriers handles track hire. The council lists toilets and water, and prohibits dogs inside the track fence.

name: Lakeside Stadium
location: Albert Park · Port Phillip · inner south
summary: Choose it when you can plan a track session around a published booking slot. State Sport Centres lists public sessions on Monday, Tuesday and Thursday afternoons and Saturday mornings, subject to events and booking availability. Check its current portal before travelling.

name: Sprint Athletics Centre
summary: Hume publishes free dawn-to-dusk entry outside exclusive bookings. A useful northern choice for counting interval laps and controlling recovery distance. Public toilets are in adjacent Craigieburn Anzac Park.

name: Edwardes Lake Park Track
summary: Darebin's March 2026 council minutes describe free, round-the-clock access. That makes it a northern option for flexible session timing. The same record notes e-bike damage and antisocial behaviour; inspect the surface and current conditions before starting fast repetitions.

name: Willinda Park
summary: Adds a measured option in the north-east. A 2023 council comparison records public use outside bookings; use the current operator's contact details to plan a session. Its published daytime hire hours describe bookings, rather than unrestricted public running hours.

name: Moonee Valley Athletics Centre
summary: An option for north-western runners who want marked repetitions. The community facility guide reports public access around exclusive club and school hire. Moonee Valley manages reserve bookings, so organised group sessions need a separate booking check.

name: Newport Park Athletics Track
spec: 400 m lane-one circuit · 8 circular lanes · synthetic
summary: The council permits public training but directs casual runners to the middle and outer lanes. Those laps are longer than 400 m, so use the correct marked start for a measured repetition. The 2026/27 rules allow 5 mm or 7 mm spikes and prohibit animals, bikes and ball games.

name: Fortitude Drive Reserve
spec: Synthetic athletics facility · public access around tenant use
summary: Included to cover the growing western suburbs. Wyndham allows public use around tenant activities. Tenant use can restrict access, especially in the evenings and on weekends. The pavilion is a later project stage; plan facilities and any group hire through the council's current updates.

name: Hagenauer Reserve / Box Hill Track
summary: An eastern alternative for measured efforts. Box Hill Athletic Club publishes facility and hire information; the public-access evidence is a 2023 council comparison. The club prohibits dogs on the track and infield, and lists floodlights and car parking.

name: Tom Kelly Athletics Track
summary: Useful for eastern-suburb intervals when the availability calendar shows public access. Club sessions have exclusive periods, so consult the published calendar rather than assuming an open gate means the track is available for your workout.

name: Duncan Mackinnon Reserve Track
summary: Glen Eira permits public running in daylight outside bookings. Its 6 am–10 pm facility hours do not grant unrestricted track access: floodlights operate for bookings, and summer club exclusions occupy several afternoons and weekend periods. Read the council's current timetable first.

name: Knox Park Athletics Centre
spec: 400 m · 8 circular lanes · Conispur SW synthetic
summary: Knox publishes daily 5 am–9 pm turnstile access, with exclusions for bookings, maintenance and mowing. The council records a Conispur SW resurfacing in 2025. A south-eastern option for planned repetitions with a clear published access window.

name: The Tan
location: Royal Botanic Gardens / Kings Domain · inner Melbourne
spec: 3.827 km official lap · gravel and sealed hill
summary: Repeated loops suit controlled aerobic running and practising uphill effort. The published Saturday 8–10 am run club and the annual Run the Tan event provide evidence of established running use. Anderson Street changes the effort of every clockwise lap.

name: Main Yarra Trail
location: CBD towards Westerfolds Park · inner and east
spec: 33 km in Parks Victoria's trail listing · lower asphalt sections
summary: A longer corridor for building a run around a chosen turnaround. Visit Victoria includes it in Melbourne's running trails, while Sri Chinmoy stages running events around Burnley. The Gipps Street ramp opened in February 2026; check current works before committing to a continuous session.

name: Albert Park Lake
location: Albert Park · Port Phillip · inner south
spec: Approximately 4.7 km lake circuit · sealed and unsealed paths
summary: A flat loop option for repeating a steady effort and returning to the same starting area. Parks Victoria recommends the park for running and documents its Saturday 8 am parkrun. Use the lake circuit distance as approximate; the event's 5 km course is a separate route.

name: Capital City Trail
location: Yarra, Merri Creek, Inner Circle, Royal Park and Docklands
spec: Approximately 29 km circuit · shared trail and street sections
summary: A varied long-run circuit, with crossings that make uninterrupted tempo work harder to organise. Melbourne Water and Merri-bek describe the route, and local running guides include it. Council planning records heavy cyclist use; leave room to share the path.

name: Bay Trail
location: Port Melbourne to Seaford · bayside corridor
spec: Choose a section and turnaround · sealed northern sections, gravel farther south
summary: A coastal option for an out-and-back long run and practising effort into changing wind. Port Phillip's event notifications document organised running along the St Kilda and Elwood foreshore. Check the event and closure notices for your chosen section before a faster session.

name: Merri Creek Trail
location: Dights Falls to the Western Ring Road · inner north and north
spec: 21 km in Merri-bek's trail description · shared creek corridor
summary: A northern option for an easy out-and-back or extending time on feet. Merri Creek Running Club's scheduled Monday 6 km sessions provide direct evidence of regular running use. Pick a turnaround for your session rather than treating the whole trail as a measured half-marathon course.
